doc: Chapter 1, Apollo 13 (April 1970), told from the beginning (issue #66; story: docs/design/story-v0.3.0.md). Every fact is from NASA's own page, its source id in docs/sources.md (S-apollo13-nasa). The cuyes never change history: they are stowaways who react; the outcome is NASA's. The prologue (who the cuyes are, why they go) is our fiction. Lines: who (a cuy or narrator), text, mood, fact + source; stage directions: set, cast, place, moves, act, acts, all, shot, cut, fx (scripts/screens/story.gd); a line with title (+ sub) and no who is a title card; a line with only wait lets the stage play.
mission: Between intro and outro the player plays the mission: build the CO2 adapter from the parts list before the CO2 climbs, then fly the return (docs/design/story-v0.3.0.md).

origin.title: Ecuador, April 1970
origin.sub: A farm on the slopes of Cotopaxi

origin.text: High in the Andes lived four cuyes who were not like the others.
Every night they climbed the hill with an old radio, to listen to the astronauts.
Houston, this is... static. Hold on. There. They are talking about the Moon again.
Next week, three astronauts fly there. Apollo 13.
origin.fact: Apollo 13 was supposed to land in the Fra Mauro area of the Moon.

origin.text: Then we fly too. Somebody has to keep an eye on them.
I will go to Houston and sit by the radio. Someone has to answer when you call.
They were small. Nobody would notice four stowaways.

pad.text: Three astronauts. One Saturn V. And a supply crate with our names on it.
pad.fact: Apollo 13 lifted off on April 11, 1970, at 1:13 p.m. CST, from Launch Pad 39A.

pad.text: Thermometer, notebook, snacks. Mostly snacks. Wait, where is Rumi?
In the tape roll. Somebody will need tape.

problem.text: Zero gravity! My snacks are orbiting me.
Next stop, the Moon. Just a little more.
I checked the tanks. Everything is fine.
Houston... we've had a problem here.
problem.fact: Swigert saw a warning light that accompanied the bang and said, "Houston, we've had a problem here."

problem.text: Wayra here! What was that bang?!
problem.fact: On April 13, 1970 (Houston time), oxygen tank no. 2 exploded, about 200,000 miles from Earth.

problem.text: I checked them. I did not check them enough.
Then no Moon landing for anyone.
problem.fact: An explosion on board forced Apollo 13 to circle the moon without landing.

problem.text: Everyone into Aquarius, the lunar module. It is our lifeboat now.
problem.fact: With the command module's power running out, the crew moved into the lunar module, their lifeboat.

lifeboat.fact: With the power off, the spacecraft got cold: 38 degrees Fahrenheit, with water on the walls.

lifeboat.text: Everything we do not need is off. We have to save power.
lifeboat.fact: All noncritical systems were turned off and energy consumption was reduced to 1/5.

lifeboat.text: The air is filling with carbon dioxide. Odyssey's filters are square. Aquarius has round holes.
lifeboat.fact: The command module's square CO2 canisters did not fit the lunar module's round openings.

lifeboat.text: Mission Control sent a recipe: plastic bags, cardboard and tape.
lifeboat.fact: Mission Control worked out an adapter from plastic bags, cardboard and tape.

fixed.fact: As they approached the Moon, a long five-minute burn sped up the return home.

home.text: Splashdown! All three astronauts are home.
home.fact: Apollo 13 splashed down on April 17, 1970, in the Pacific Ocean near Samoa; the recovery ship was USS Iwo Jima.

home.text: We never landed on the Moon. But everybody came back. That counts.
Next time, can we just land somewhere?
Mars. On airbags. What could go wrong.
